results.name: T-72
results.description:
I decided to drop my grand ambitions and start with a simple browser game, I ran tests on WebGL and found that it really dislikes a large number of polygons, FPS drops start from 300-500k polygons, but how to make a game with a large number of units on the map? at least 300 units that will fight, and how to make a variety of different vehicles and not spend all the time of your life on it? I chose a simple low poly style, with flat texturing, and with shade smoothing, so that polygons would not cut your eyes

The main rule for vehicle - No more than 1000 tris, even if you have 1001 polygons - NO! no more than 1000 in principle
Flat texturing with 64x64 texture which has different colors, with this you can use only one material for all units in the game, which will increase optimization

About T-72, the most difficult thing here was to make a tower in Low-Poly style, it is different on every bluprint

results.name: Wolseley 1000 Saloon lowpoly for 3D-printing
results.description:
This work is based on a Sketchup-file. Unfortunately I don´t remember the name of its author. Anyway, thanks for the great model! Several years ago I converted and repaired it into a watertight STL-file. Sadly the resolution of the model is only useful for printing in small scales.

My purpose is to provide watertight STL-files for you, which can easily be modified for 3D-printing, according to your references. Therefore, most of my models are not repaired into one single shell. This may be a bit more difficult for the preparation of the build, but helps you a lot, if you want to personalize the model. E.g. if you want to seperate parts, such as wheels or to remove delicate details like wipers etc.

Before printing, please check out if you have to modify the model, depending on the favored size of your print and the requirements of your printer. I hope you enjoy it. Happy printing!

If you are going to print this model, please feel free to share your experiences about its printability in the comments.

results.name: Aplysia californica
results.description:
On a hike at Wilder Ranch today I came across a number of these creatures scattered across the beach. They are a type of sea slug known as a sea hare. They looked like brown lumps of goo with spots, antennae, and ruffles. Luckily the tide was coming up, so most of them ended up back in the water unharmed.

Here is the Monterey Bay Aquarium info on sea hares: http://www.montereybayaquarium.org/animal-guide/invertebrates/sea-hare

The photos for this model were captured with my iPhone.
![Alt text](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/544825ade4b002e9ed1c7497/t/55de8e1ae4b07afa63298f95/1440648739062/beach?format=1000w)

results.name: T 25K WJ_Glarus v. 1.0
results.description:
Letter: T Version: 25000 Polygons Font: WJ_Glarus v. 1.0

Introducing WJ_Glarus , a beautiful 3D font created using Cinema4D, Illustrator, and Stable Diffusion. This font is licensed under Creative Commons and is available for free download, making it a fantastic resource for designers and creatives everywhere.

With 52 letters in the English alphabet, WJ_Glarus v. 1.0 is a versatile choice for a wide range of projects.

What sets WJ_Glarus v. 1.0 apart is its flexibility. It comes in three different versions, each with a different polygon count to suit different project requirements. The low-poly version, with only 1000 polygons, is perfect for simulations and games, while the mid-poly version, with 3000 polygons, is great for projects that require more detail. And for those who need the ultimate level of detail, the high-poly version with 25000 polygons captures every curve and detail in stunning 3D. Peace and happy design Wendelin Jacober

results.name: 3D model of Gunung Rinjani
results.description:
Gunung Rinjani is an active arc volcano that dominates the topography of Lombok, Indonesia. It produced the 1257 AD Samalas eruption, which was one of the largest Holocene eruptions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1257_Samalas_eruption).

This vertically exaggerated model was produced using tectoplot (https://github.com/kyleedwardbradley/tectoplot/). Topo data are from GMRT and SRTM, and the contours are baked into the texture.

tectoplot -r 115.8 116.8 -9 -8 -t BEST -pgs 0.5 -t0 -tn 1000 -geotiff -makeply topoexag 2.5 maxsize 800 sidebox 10 gray maptiff -n

results.name: Appalachian valley and ridge folds, Pennsylvania
results.description:
The Appalachian Valley and Ridge province (https://www.nps.gov/articles/valleyandridgeprovince.htm) is an excellent example of the importance of bedrock geological structure and stratigraphy for the present-day landscape. Differential erodability of the Paleozoic sedimentary rocks, which were tightly folded during compressional mountain building, has created the beautiful and complex modern landscape.

This model was made using tectoplot and USGS 1/3 arcsecond terrain. Topography is vertically exaggerated by a factor of 2.

tectoplot -r -77.9 -77.6 40.6 40.9 -t ~/Downloads/USGS_13_n41w078.tif -t0 -tcpt R1 -tr -makeply maxsize 1000 sidebox 2 white topoexag 2

results.name: Redwood trunk
results.description:
This is a very small part of a very big tree at Henry Cowell Redwoods State Park in Felton, California. This particular tree is over 17 feet (5 meters) wide and 270 feet (83 meters) tall. It is called "The Giant". Redwoods are the tallest species of tree in the world, and some of the trees in the park are nearly 2000 years old. My mind is blown every time I visit.

This was shot with my iPhone in 28 photos. The lighting was not ideal, but I'm not sure that it gets any better in the forest. :-)

Here's the park website: http://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=546

And here is the Wikipedia page on coast redwoods: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequoia_sempervirens

![Alt text](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/544825ade4b002e9ed1c7497/t/55df7ce5e4b0228f9cdebf5b/1440709871192/?format=1000w)

results.name: Lawetlat'la / Louwala-Clough / Mount St. Helens
results.description:
This great continental arc volcano erupted spectacularly on May 18, 1980 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_St.Helens), leaving a wide region of destruction from the flank collapse landslide, pyroclastic flows, and lahars. 

This model was produced using a 1/3 arcsecond DEM (USGS) and Sentinel cloud-free imagery (EOX IT Services GmbH), using the open-source script tectoplot (https://github.com/kyleedwardbradley/tectoplot. 

The command used was

tectoplot -r -122.31 -122.06 46.12 46.30 -t ~/Downloads/USGS_13_n47w123_20210615.tif -pgs 0.5 -t0 -tgam 0.5 -tshad 45 5 -tsent 0.1 -makeply topoexag 1 maxsize 1000 sidebox 2 lightgray
